newsitem.title: UK: Britain may send icy undercarriage stowaway home.
newsitem.headline: Britain may send icy undercarriage stowaway home.

text.p: An Indian who miraculously survived as a stowaway in the frozen undercarriage of a jumbo jet flying from Delhi to London is unlikely to be allowed to stay in Britain, a minister said on Tuesday.

Pardeep Saini, 23, endured temperatures as low as minus 60 C (-76F) during the flight last October. His younger brother Vijay froze to death, his body falling to the ground as the jet's wheel were lowered for landing.
Junior interior minister Mike O'Brien said he had received a report from an immigration adjudicator saying that Saini does not qualify for political asylum.
Saini claims that he faces persecution if he is forced to return to Punjab because of allegations that he supports Sikh separatist extremists.
O'Brien said he would now consider Saini's removal from Britain, although he would take into account reports on his medical condition.
"The death of Mr Saini's brother was certainly tragic, but I would be reluctant to reward someone for using extreme methods for avoiding immigration control," O'Brien said in a statement.
When Saini was found wandering on the tarmac at London's Heathrow airport in October, doctors said it was a miracle he had survived the harsh conditions of the flight.
They said he probably lost consciousness and went into a state of suspended animation which helped to prevent brain damage.
Piara Khabra, member of parliament for Southall, the area of west London where Saini has been living with an uncle, called on the government to allow him to stay.
"Pardeep is clearly an amazing human being and deserves a chance," he told London's Evening Standard newspaper.
